title: Fleet Recall / Dependencies
description: Live CockroachDB transaction/readiness and local embedding metrics. Retries, latency distributions, outcomes and numeric work units preserve operation boundaries and keep missing observations distinct from zero.

options.content:
**Live processes only.** Every query uses `job="fleet-recall"`; scheduled worker textfile snapshots are excluded. Select a deployment and instance to isolate a bottleneck. Blank panels mean missing samples, an unobserved boundary, or no activity in the rate window—not a healthy result.

**Scope.** Database timings cover health checks and the shared serializable transaction helper, not every SQL query. `embedding/local_batch` is model encoding; `embedding/embed` includes blocking-pool scheduling and vector validation. They can nest: never add their operation counts, durations, or in-flight values.

panels.title: Live scrape targets
panels.description: Count of currently reachable selected live metrics targets. This is exporter reachability, not database readiness. Missing targets remain no data.

panels.title: Observed health success
panels.description: Successful observed health checks / all checks in the selected range. Health checks are on demand/startup, not a continuous uptime probe. No checks produce no value.

panels.title: Transaction p95
panels.description: Rolling p95 over the rate interval, aggregated across selected targets, including retries, backoff and unsuccessful operations. The 2 s color threshold is illustrative, not a service objective.

panels.title: Attempts / logical operation
panels.description: Rate of attempt starts / rate of terminal logical transactions. Invalid policy calls are excluded. Near 1 means one attempt in steady traffic; completion lag and in-flight work can cause transient values below 1 or spikes. This is not an exact per-request retry distribution.

panels.title: Retry exhaustions · range
panels.description: Estimated serialization retry exhaustions in the selected time range. increase() adjusts for observed resets and extrapolates boundaries; early events before the first scrape can be missed. Investigate persistent contention before increasing retry limits.

panels.title: Accepted embeddings · range
panels.description: Estimated count of vectors accepted by the projection provider during the selected range. This is not all texts encoded: query encoding also contributes to local_batch/texts.

panels.title: Serializable transactions · one logical operation includes every retry
Transaction latency · p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Per-instance histogram percentiles include connection acquisition, setup, body, commit, retry backoff and unsuccessful completions. Estimates are bucket-based; isolate an instance before attributing a tail spike to the database.

panels.title: Logical transaction outcomes
panels.description: One terminal observation per logical transaction. Error includes begin/setup/body/commit failures and retry exhaustion; cancellation does not prove rollback. Invalid denotes an invalid retry policy.

panels.title: Actual retries · body and commit
panels.description: Retry counters increase after backoff immediately before a fresh attempt. Body and commit reasons are separate; cancellation during backoff is not counted as an executed retry.

panels.title: Retry amplification by instance
panels.description: Attempt-start rate divided by completed logical-transaction rate, excluding invalid policies. Compare with in-flight work: different start/completion times make this approximate during ramps and slow operations. No completed operations yields no value.

panels.title: Active logical transactions
panels.description: Current shared-helper operations, including pool acquisition and retry backoff. This gauge is not the number of open database connections or individual SQL statements.

panels.title: Attempts and terminal operations
panels.description: Compare all attempt starts with terminal logical operations. The gap reflects retries and timing differences. Both series are live-process rates; invalid-policy terminal calls are excluded.

panels.title: Exhaustions by instance · selected range
panels.description: Window increase per instance. Any positive value warrants inspecting contention and transaction duration. A zero is meaningful only for an observed retry counter; absent series remain absent.

panels.title: Database health · observed checks, not continuous database uptime
Health-check success fraction
panels.description: Rolling successful / all observed health checks by instance. A process may only check readiness at startup; missing activity is not evidence of health. Verify current readiness separately when these panels have no recent observations.

panels.title: Health-check outcomes
panels.description: Observed check completions per second. Errors include connection failures and missing required database schema/capabilities. Compare with exporter reachability; an up scrape does not imply database readiness.

panels.title: Health-check p95 duration
panels.description: Includes the scoped corpus liveness query and capability/schema checks. It is not a lightweight database ping or a timer for all read queries.

panels.title: Embedding boundaries · inspect local_batch and embed separately
Encoding and projection measure different work

options.content:
`local_batch` counts model encode calls and records `texts` after a successful encode. It includes query and corpus encoding, and does not validate vectors. `embed` measures one projection-provider call, including blocking-pool queueing and validation; its `embeddings` unit counts accepted vectors.

A projection call can contain a local batch. Compare the two boundaries to locate queueing or validation cost, but do not sum them or divide their throughput to claim a model acceptance percentage. Their input populations differ. Panics are errors; malformed/empty/non-finite/zero vectors are invalid provider outcomes.

panels.title: Model encoding · p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Latency of embedding/local_batch only, across selected instances. Percentiles include unsuccessful completions. Compare corresponding quantiles rather than subtracting percentiles to estimate queueing time.

panels.title: Model encoding · latency distribution
panels.description: Pre-bucketed histogram rates for this boundary only. Grafana converts cumulative Prometheus buckets to per-bucket values. Color is operations/second; vertical axis is seconds. Finite buckets stop at 300 s; the percentile panels retain +Inf observations. No observations remain empty.

panels.title: Model encoding · outcomes
panels.description: Terminal embedding/local_batch outcomes only. Zero means an observed counter with no recent increments; missing samples remain empty. local_batch can succeed even when embed later rejects the vector.

panels.title: Projection provider · p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Latency of embedding/embed only, across selected instances. Percentiles include unsuccessful completions. Compare corresponding quantiles rather than subtracting percentiles to estimate queueing time.

panels.title: Projection provider · latency distribution
panels.description: Pre-bucketed histogram rates for this boundary only. Grafana converts cumulative Prometheus buckets to per-bucket values. Color is operations/second; vertical axis is seconds. Finite buckets stop at 300 s; the percentile panels retain +Inf observations. No observations remain empty.

panels.title: Projection provider · outcomes
panels.description: Terminal embedding/embed outcomes only. Zero means an observed counter with no recent increments; missing samples remain empty. local_batch can succeed even when embed later rejects the vector.

panels.title: Error fraction by boundary
panels.description: Errors include an encoder panic; inspect sanitized completion events and model/runtime health. Each operation uses its own terminal-call denominator. No calls produce no fraction; boundaries are never summed.

panels.title: Invalid-vector fraction by boundary
panels.description: Vector validity is checked by embed; a zero local_batch invalid fraction does not prove usable output vectors. Each operation uses its own terminal-call denominator. No calls produce no fraction; boundaries are never summed.

panels.title: Successful input texts and accepted vectors
panels.description: Texts are counted after successful local_batch encoding; embeddings after embed validation. Query texts are included only in local_batch. These are two separate measures, not a funnel, yield ratio, or total throughput to be summed.

panels.title: Active embedding operations by boundary
panels.description: Separate gauges for local encoding and projection-provider work. One request can occupy both boundaries; adding them would double-count nested work. A dropped async provider call may finish while its blocking encode continues.

panels.title: Embedding p95 by instance and boundary
panels.description: Use instance selection to separate slow hosts from a shared model or database bottleneck. Includes failed operations and requires observations in the current rate interval.

panels.title: Embedding outcomes · selected range
panels.description: Estimated terminal calls by boundary and outcome in the selected range; increase() extrapolates scrape boundaries. Keep local_batch and embed values separate because they can describe nested work.

options.content:
**Transactions:** Rising retries plus longer transactions suggest contention or long work inside a transaction. Inspect CockroachDB diagnostics and concurrent writers before increasing retry limits. Retry exhaustion is a terminal error; cancellation alone does not prove a mutation rolled back.

**Embedding:** Compare local encoding with the projection-provider boundary. A slow provider with normal encoding can indicate blocking-pool queueing; invalid outcomes indicate unusable model output. Use operation completion events for time/operation correlation without adding content or model identifiers as metric labels.

**Collection:** Counters reset at restart; rates handle observed resets. Events before the first scrape can be missed. Heatmap buckets are estimates; no-data remains distinct from zero. Threshold colors are illustrative starting points, not established service objectives. For scheduled workers, use the Workers dashboard and read textfile counters directly.
